title: Ricci-flow curve control: mathematical blueprint
scope: A Lean formalization of uniform length and total-curvature estimates along existing smooth immersed closed curve flows, including arbitrary static one-dimensional factor metrics.
dependency_semantics: Edges record selected mathematical prerequisites used to organize the exposition.

notation.time: a <= t <= b inside the supplied Ricci-flow time set; high-order evolution is proved at interior times.
notation.space: x is a period-one real parameter; D_s = v^{-1}D_x.
notation.metric: All tensor norms, pairings and curve quantities use the actual g(t) or its genuine product metric.
notation.curvature_sign: rm uses the upstream intrinsic four-form; its conversion from the opposite-sign chart curvature operator is explicitly proved.
notation.constants: B bounds Ricci, K bounds Riemann curvature, D bounds covariant Ricci; A=max(6B+2K,6D), C=A/2+B.
notation.regularization: epsilon > 0; Theta_epsilon is compared first and epsilon tends to zero afterwards.

references.title: Correction to Section 19.2 of Ricci Flow and the Poincaré Conjecture, Lemmas 0.1–0.4
references.role: Corrected mathematical source; spatial connection route is an adaptation.

references.title: Perelman, Finite extinction time, sections 2–3
references.role: The finite-extinction argument in which these curve estimates are used.

references.title: frenzymath/Poincare-Conjecture, pinned geometric libraries
references.role: Reused upstream Riemannian geometry and Ricci-flow infrastructure.

references.title: Frozen upstream curve-shrinking-estimates blueprint
references.role: Proof plan for the curve-estimate module.

references.title: mathlib, pinned commit 520045ab14e26149ee970e2e617ca04b09bde5d6
references.role: Reused analysis, linear algebra and manifold infrastructure.

nodes.title: Actual Ricci flow and immersed closed curve flow
nodes.explanation: Assume a smooth metric family and a jointly smooth immersed periodic curve family. The time equations use derivatives within the given time set.

contribution.detail: Reuses the upstream Ricci-flow predicate and adds the actual periodic curve-flow interface.

scope_caveats: Existing smooth flows are inputs; existence and continuation belong to the surrounding theory.
Higher evolution identities hold at interior times.

nodes.title: Intrinsic curve geometry and moving measure
nodes.math_statement: X=c_x,\quad v=|X|_g,\quad S=v^{-1}X,\quad H=D_sS,\quad q=|H|_g^2,\quad ds=v\,dx.\qquad L=\int_0^1v\,dx,\quad\Theta=\int_0^1\sqrt q\,v\,dx.
nodes.explanation: Covariant derivatives use moving tangent fields in a fixed valid chart. Lengths and contractions use the evolving metric.

contribution.detail: Defines the geometric quantities and integral densities used by the project.

scope_caveats: Closed curves are represented by period-one real parametrizations; self-intersections are allowed.

nodes.title: Speed and unit-tangent evolution
nodes.explanation: The flow equations imply the mixed covariant derivative identity and hence the speed law.

contribution.detail: Derives speed and tangent evolution from mixed derivatives and metric variation.

scope_caveats: Classical time derivatives are asserted at interior times.

nodes.title: Time variation of the Levi-Civita connection
nodes.explanation: Differentiate Christoffel symbols in time at a fixed spatial chart point, then lower the index using g(t).

contribution.detail: Adapts the spacetime calculation to the time-varying spatial connection.

scope_caveats: Lowering means g(t) applied to the connection derivative. The metric-variation term is handled separately.

nodes.title: Corrected squared-curvature evolution
nodes.explanation: The given flows determine curvature-vector evolution, the required covariant regularity, connection lowering and curvature-sign conversion.

contribution.detail: Formalizes the corrected evolution through an equivalent purely spatial connection calculation.

scope_caveats: P is the spatial normal projection; the spacetime projection has an additional component.
The squared-curvature PDE is derived from the flow inputs.

nodes.title: Spatial Kato inequality
nodes.explanation: Metric Cauchy–Schwarz and covariant differentiability give gradient control at curvature zeros.

contribution.detail: Proves the metric gradient identities and derives their regularity from the flow.

scope_caveats: The argument uses q and its derivatives, including at q=0.

nodes.title: Uniform ambient error coefficients
nodes.explanation: B, K and D bound Ricci, Riemann curvature and covariant Ricci evaluations in metric norms.

contribution.detail: Extracts explicit ambient-only coefficients from every corrected term.

scope_caveats: This layer takes tensor bounds as inputs; compactness later supplies them.

nodes.title: Positive regularization and scalar PDE
nodes.explanation: The chain rule and Kato cancellation retain the linear-curvature error while regularization handles q=0.

contribution.detail: Proves the regularized analytic inequality and applies it to the geometric PDE.

scope_caveats: The local analytic lemma takes a scalar PDE and differentiability hypotheses; the geometric theorem proves these inputs.

nodes.title: Moving arclength integrals and periodic cancellation
nodes.explanation: Joint smoothness supplies parameter-integral differentiability. Periodicity cancels the integrated arclength diffusion; the cubic term is absorbed by the moving density.

contribution.detail: Applies parameter integration and FTC to the density v, with the needed regularity proved in the assembly.

scope_caveats: Domination for fixed epsilon may depend on epsilon; the comparison coefficients are uniform in epsilon.
Time differentiation applies to L and regularized total curvature. An a.e. derivative interface for Theta requires a further theorem.

nodes.title: Comparison from interior derivatives and closed continuity
nodes.explanation: Interior derivative comparison and closed-interval continuity carry the initial bound to both time endpoints.

contribution.detail: Adapts the blueprint’s AC/a.e. comparison to interior derivatives and closed continuity.

scope_caveats: Initial-endpoint continuity suffices; an initial derivative or negative-time extension is unnecessary.

nodes.title: Remove regularization after comparison
nodes.explanation: The already-proved comparison passes to the limit at its two endpoints.

contribution.detail: Provides quantitative integral error and a limit interface for the comparison.

scope_caveats: Limits are taken in the endpoint comparison. Local absolute continuity of Theta remains a separate result.

nodes.title: Actual geometric length and total-curvature bound
nodes.explanation: The flows and ambient bounds supply every scalar hypothesis in the analytic comparison.

contribution.detail: Combines geometry and analysis to propagate initial bounds over arbitrary curve indices.

scope_caveats: Inputs are the flows and ambient tensor bounds; the differential and integral estimates follow from them.

nodes.title: Weighted curvature-energy control
nodes.math_statement: \mathcal E(t)=\int q\,ds,\qquad\int_a^b e^{-B(t-a)}\mathcal E(t)\,dt\le L(a)-e^{-B(b-a)}L(b).\quad B\ge0\Rightarrow\int_a^b\mathcal E(t)\,dt\le e^{B(b-a)}L(a)-L(b).
nodes.explanation: The negative curvature-energy term in the length derivative yields an exponential-weighted integral estimate for downstream good-time selection.

contribution.detail: Proves weighted and unweighted energy estimates for the actual curve flow.

scope_caveats: The roots assume one lower Ricci bound for all ambient unit vectors over [a,b]. Upper Ricci, Riemann and covariant Ricci bounds are unnecessary. The unweighted version requires B >= 0.

nodes.title: Ambient bounds from compact base geometry
nodes.math_statement: M\text{ compact},\ g(t)\text{ jointly smooth on }[a,b]\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\exists B,K,D\ge0:\ |\mathrm{Ric}|\le B,\ |\mathrm{Rm}|\le K,\ |\nabla\mathrm{Ric}|\le D.
nodes.explanation: Finite compact chart covers, coefficient continuity, inverse-Gram control and tensor expansion yield bounds in actual metric norms.

contribution.detail: Constructs the uniform constants used by the compact-base theorem.

scope_caveats: These are multilinear evaluation bounds. The base manifold is compact; the static factor may be noncompact.

nodes.title: Genuine product metric in a Hilbert model
nodes.explanation: An identity-on-points model change transports the product metric to WithLp 2 and preserves the fiber metric.

contribution.detail: Reuses DCProductMetric and proves Hilbert-model transport and metric fiber isometry.

scope_caveats: The Hilbert model is WithLp 2; the ordinary product retains its max norm. Geometric pairings use g and h.

nodes.title: Every genuine one-dimensional factor is flat
nodes.explanation: Alternation and one-dimensional linear dependence annihilate curvature. Ricci vanishes as a field before taking its covariant derivative.

contribution.detail: Derives one-dimensional flatness for every smooth Riemannian metric.

scope_caveats: This result applies to supplied one-dimensional geometry; circle atlases and specific scaled metrics are handled separately.

nodes.title: Actual product curvature and Ricci splitting
nodes.explanation: Christoffel coefficients and their spatial derivatives split on open chart targets. The signed intrinsic curvature bridge and the metric fiber isometry then give curvature and Ricci splitting.

contribution.detail: Derives connection, chart curvature, intrinsic curvature and Ricci splitting from the product metric.

scope_caveats: U_j denotes the proved tangent projection with its specified fiber metric.

nodes.title: Actual covariant Ricci splitting
nodes.explanation: Differentiate the Ricci coefficient splitting on a valid chart germ, add both Christoffel corrections, and identify the intrinsic tensor on arbitrary vectors.

contribution.detail: Proves covariant Ricci splitting through Fréchet differentiation and trilinear tensor identities.

scope_caveats: Coefficient and covariant-derivative splitting are conclusions of the geometric proof.

nodes.title: Static one-dimensional products solve Ricci flow
nodes.explanation: Pullbacks and sums give joint within smoothness. Fixed-vector time differentiation uses the base equation and the static factor.

contribution.detail: Proves the product Ricci-flow equation, including within derivatives at time endpoints.

scope_caveats: h may vary with an external index, but is static in Ricci-flow time.

nodes.title: Unchanged base coefficients for every static factor metric
nodes.math_statement: (B,K,D)\text{ bound }g(t),\ \dim N=1\quad\Longrightarrow\quad(B,K,D)\text{ also bound }g(t)\oplus h\text{ for every }h.
nodes.explanation: One-dimensional vanishing removes the factor tensor terms. The base projection decreases metric length, preserving the same constants.

contribution.detail: Preserves all three ambient coefficients independently of factor scale or injectivity radius.

scope_caveats: The constant-preservation theorem itself works from supplied base bounds; compactness constructs them for the final root.

nodes.title: Compact-base uniform estimates, including every positive scale
nodes.explanation: For a compact base Ricci flow on [a,b], choose constants before all static one-dimensional factor metrics, curve families and initial bounds. Curves are existing smooth immersed periodic solutions. The positive-scale corollary permits arbitrary metrics indexed by lambda > 0.

contribution.detail: Combines compact ambient bounds, product geometry and corrected comparison into the uniform estimate.

scope_caveats: Constants are independent of the entire metric family, including arbitrarily small positive scales; scale regularity is unnecessary.
Concrete AddCircle atlases, ramp existence, a local-AC/a.e. interface for Theta, and the remaining finite-extinction argument require further input or results.
Uniform initial length and total-curvature bounds are inputs.

nodes.title: Constructed scaled metrics and a full-interval application
nodes.explanation: Construct the scaled Riemannian metric and apply exponential monotonicity to obtain bounds uniform in positive scale, curve index and time.

contribution.detail: Constructs metric scaling and applies the uniform estimate over the full time interval.

scope_caveats: Inputs are the one-dimensional manifold, its starting metric, existing smooth curve flows and uniform initial bounds.
The construction uses positive scales. A concrete AddCircle atlas, ramps and solution existence belong to the surrounding application; no metric at scale zero is constructed.
